findings.evidence_dynamic: Header 'X-Frame-Options' is missing. Risk: Clickjacking attacks — page can be embedded in iframes
findings.remediation: To remediate the X-Frame-Options header vulnerability, set the 'X-Frame-Options' header to a suitable value such as 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN' to prevent clickjacking attacks. This can be achieved by adding the following code to the web server configuration or application: `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'DENY'`. For example, in Apache HTTP Server, add the line `Header set X-Frame-Options "DENY"` to the server configuration file.

findings.evidence_dynamic: Header 'Content-Security-Policy' is missing. Risk: No XSS mitigation policy — scripts from any source allowed
findings.remediation: To remediate the Content-Security-Policy header vulnerability, add the 'Content-Security-Policy' header to your server's response with a policy that defines allowed sources for scripts, such as 'default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://example.com'. For example, in Apache, you can add the following line to your configuration file: `Header set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://example.com"`. This will restrict script execution to only scripts from the same origin and https://example.com, mitigating the risk of XSS attacks.

findings.evidence_dynamic: Header 'Strict-Transport-Security' is missing. Risk: HTTP downgrade attacks — HTTPS not enforced
findings.remediation: To remediate the missing Strict-Transport-Security header, configure your web server to include this header in its responses. For example, in Apache, add the following line to your configuration file: `Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"`. This sets the Strict-Transport-Security header with a maximum age of one year, enforcing HTTPS for the domain and its subdomains.

findings.evidence_dynamic: Header 'X-Content-Type-Options' is missing. Risk: MIME-type sniffing — browser may misinterpret content
findings.remediation: To remediate the missing X-Content-Type-Options header vulnerability, set the 'X-Content-Type-Options' header to 'nosniff' in your server configuration or application code. For example, in Apache, add the line 'Header set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"' to your httpd.conf file or .htaccess file. In Node.js with Express, use the line 'app.use((req, res, next) => { res.setHeader("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff"); next(); });' to set the header for all responses.

findings.evidence_dynamic: Header 'Referrer-Policy' is missing. Risk: URL data leaked to third parties via Referer header
findings.remediation: To remediate the Referrer-Policy header vulnerability, add the 'Referrer-Policy' header to your HTTP responses with a suitable directive, such as 'same-origin' or 'no-referrer'. This can be achieved by setting the header in your web server configuration or application code, for example: `response.setHeader("Referrer-Policy", "same-origin")`. In Apache, you can add the header using the `Header` directive: `Header always set Referrer-Policy "same-origin"`.

findings.evidence_dynamic: Header 'Permissions-Policy' is missing. Risk: No browser feature restrictions defined
findings.remediation: To remediate the Permissions-Policy header vulnerability, add the 'Permissions-Policy' header to your server's response with the desired feature policies. For example, you can set it in Apache using the `Header` directive: `Header set Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()"`. This will restrict browser features such as geolocation, microphone, and camera access for the specified URL.
